title: On-call Incident Playbook: RBAC v2 & Evidence Automation
content:
Purpose:
This is the working on-call playbook for incidents that touch RBAC v2 controls, audit log schema breakage, evidence collection automation, and SIEM export issues. Focus: preserve evidence, minimize blast radius, ensure correct role enforcement, and restore observability to downstream tooling (SIEM/IR pipeline).

Scope:
- Incidents where RBAC decisions are incorrect (grant/deny mismatch, policy regression, unintended escalation).
- Audit log schema changes or missing fields that break ingestion / SIEM parsing.
- Evidence automation failures (collector not bundling artifacts, signed evidence missing).
- SIEM export outages (export jobs failing, mapping drift).

Quick triage checklist (first 10 mins):
1) Triage owner (oncall sec) acknowledges in #sec-oncall and sets incident channel.
2) Severity estimate: S0 (data exfil / active abuse) | S1 (elevated privileges) | S2 (observability degradation) | S3 (policy dev/false positives). Pick highest applicable.
3) Snapshot impacted services: RBAC service, AuthN proxy, Audit ingestion lambda, SIEM forwarder, Evidence automation runner.
4) Run safety mitigation: if active abuse suspected, rotate service tokens for affected services and apply emergency deny on affected principle(s).

Who does what (roles):
- Oncall Sec (pri): lead triage, coordinate mitigations, escalate to SRE/product.
- Identity Engineer (ie): inspect RBAC v2 policy templates, rollout logs, recent PRs.
- IR Engineer / Forensics (ir): collect evidence, preserve chain-of-custody, run automation collector.
- Observability SRE (obs): check SIEM ingestion, Splunk/Datadog forwarder, forwarding queues.
- Product Owner (po): review policy intents and approve rollback if needed.

Immediate commands & queries (copy/paste):
- API: RBAC decision audit for user X (use request_id when available):
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' 
    'https://auth.redwood-inference.internal/api/v2/audit/decisions?actor_id=USER_ID&since=2026-02-10T00:00:00Z'
  # returns list of decision records with fields (request_id, actor_id, actor_roles, resource, action, decision, policy_version)

- Splunk SPL (audit log hits last 60m where policy_version absent):
  index=audit_logs sourcetype=rbac_v2 | where isnull(policy_version) OR policy_version=="" | table _time request_id actor_id actor_roles resource action outcome field_changes

- Elastic/KQL (if using ES):
  event.dataset: "redwood.audit" AND (NOT exists:policy.version OR policy.version:"") | sort @timestamp desc | limit 50

- Evidence automation collector (local run):
  # quick-run: gather latest logs + config + evidence bundle for request_id
  ./scripts/collect_evidence.sh --request $REQUEST_ID --output /tmp/evidence-$REQUEST_ID.tar.gz
  # script will: call audit API, fetch service logs from logging-export, snapshot RBAC policy repo commit, export SIEM ingestion job status JSON, sign bundle with KMS key id=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/sec/cryptoKeys/evidence

Audit log schema notes (fields to validate when troubleshooting ingestion):
- required fields: request_id, timestamp, service, actor_id, actor_roles, resource_type, resource_id, action, decision (allow/deny), policy_version, outcome, request_context (ip, user_agent), trace_id
- optional helpful fields: policy_diff, rule_id, policy_commit, node_id, k8s_namespace, container_id
- common failures we see: missing policy_version after hotfix, actor_roles array collapsed to string, trace_id null due to proxy drop

SIEM export troubleshooting steps:
1) Check forwarder status (k8s job / lambda): kubectl -n observability get pods -l app=siem-forwarder -o wide OR aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name siem-forwarder-prod
2) Confirm last successful export timestamp (S3 / ELB metrics).
3) If parsing errors: pull raw audit object and run local parser: python tools/siem_parser.py --input raw.json --schema schemas/audit_v2.yaml --strict
4) If schema drift detected, create temporary mapper in SIEM (Splunk props/transforms) to keep dashboards working while we fix producer.

Mitigations (short-term):
- For RBAC bad-enforcement: apply emergency policy rollback to last-known-good policy_version (use admin console or API). Document reason and time.
- For audit schema regression: re-enable legacy exporter with compatibility shim (forward raw->legacy) OR patch producer to include missing fields.
- For SIEM ingestion outages: switch forwarder to fallback bucket and re-ingest backlog with retention script.

Evidence collection & chain of custody (must do for S0/S1):
- Tag incident id on all artifacts: INCIDENT=INC-YYYYMMDD-###
- Use automated collector to fetch: policy repo commit, audit events for request ids, service logs (±5min around event), raw network captures if applicable, siem-forwarder logs, container snapshots (image digest), and KMS signing metadata.
- Save bundle to secure evidence bucket (s3://redwood-evidence/<incident>/bundle.tar.gz) with ACL restricted to ir-team and sec-leads.
- Note collector artifacts in incident timeline with checksums (sha256) and signer key id.

Post-incident tasks (security postmortem template):
- Write a timeline with timestamps and owner annotations.
- Root cause: categorize (policy bug, deployment/config drift, missing tests, parsing issue, infra outage).
- Impact: list affected customers, tokens rotated, data exposures.
- Corrective actions: short-term rollback + long-term fixes (tests, schema validation, SIEM contract), owners and ETA.
- QA: add unit/regression tests to policy CI, add synthetic SIEM ingestion test to CI (nightly), and a canary pipeline for RBAC rollouts.

Detection rules & alerts to add (examples):
- Alert: Audit records missing policy_version for >1% of RBAC decisions over 10m window -> Pager to sec-oncall.
- Alert: Spike in allow decisions for high-privileged actions (create_service_token, iam:impersonate) -> S1.
- Alert: SIEM forwarder failing 5 consecutive exports -> runbook auto-trigger.

Automation notes / TODOs (working list):
- [ ] Harden collect_evidence.sh to support incremental pulls (resume on failure).
- [x] Add schema strictness toggle to siem_parser.py (PR merged: #78).
- [ ] Create a RBAC rollout canary that exercises deny/allow simulation with canary users.
- [ ] Add signed evidence manifest (manifest.json + sha256s) to the bundle for legal.

Known gotchas / past incidents (short notes):
- 2025-04: policy template change removed policy_version field in producer resulting in 72h dashboards outage. Learned: add contract tests on push to prod.
- 2025-11: evidence runner crashed due to role boundary change; collector used broad role instead of least-privilege. Fix: limited role for collector and cross-account read-only flows.

Open questions for product/security sync:
- Do we enforce schema contract at compile time for RBAC template builds? (still debated)
- What is maximum acceptable SIEM ingestion lag before we declare S1? (proposed: 30m)

Appendix: sample incident timeline snippet (example)
- 2026-02-10T08:12:03Z - Alert: missing policy_version (splunk) -> page sec-oncall
- 2026-02-10T08:13:00Z - Oncall acknowledged (Priya Shah)
- 2026-02-10T08:20:31Z - Short mitigation: rollback to policy_version v2026-02-09-21:14 (Marco Diaz)
- 2026-02-10T08:35:00Z - Evidence bundle created /tmp/evidence-req1234.tar.gz (IR engine)
- 2026-02-10T09:02:12Z - SIEM ingestion resumed after forwarder patch (obs)
notes: Informal doc: rough runbook and checklist; meant to be iterated. Keep this in drive (working copy) and port to Confluence after final review.
